introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2021. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all tasks (Task I, Task II, Task III) in this question paper.**

The booklet reproduced here contains three versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two and Group Three (booklets GCE/P/2021/0595/3/C/Grp 1, Grp 2 and Grp 3). Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing, 20 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks) and Task III (reading and running a short C or Pascal program, 10 marks). A candidate works on one group only (the printed paper does not say how the groups are allotted).

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The working files named in the tasks (the picture 'CornerShop' found on the desktop, Group Two Task II) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

questions.enonce_markdown: Launch either a C or Pascal program development environment, and key in the corresponding program. Compile the program. If any errors, keep correcting and compiling until all the errors are corrected. Save as Task 3.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Open a C or a Pascal development environment (an IDE with a compiler), create a new source file, key in the program of your choice **exactly as printed** and compile it (*Build* / *Compile*, often *F9*).

- Check while typing: the semicolons, the braces `{ }` of the `while` in C or `begin ... end;` and the final `END.` in Pascal, `while (i <= 3)` with its parentheses in C and `while i <= 3 do` in Pascal, `i = i+1;` in C and `i := i+1;` in Pascal, `&num` in `scanf`, the `\n` in the format strings.
- Read the compiler messages, correct the error at the line indicated and compile again until there is no error.

Then *File* > **Save As**, file name **Task 3**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Run the program and provide 25, 300, and 4500 when prompted for a number, pressing the <Enter> key after each number is entered. Write the output you observe.  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The `while` loop runs while `i <= 3`, so three times (`i` = 1, 2, 3). In each pass: print `i`, ask for a number of metres, `km = num / 1000` (whole kilometres, quotient), `m = num % 1000` (metres left, remainder), print the result and a blank line, then `i = i + 1`. Trace (Python simulation):

| `i` | `num` | `km` = quotient | `m` = remainder |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 25 | 0 | 25 |
| 2 | 300 | 0 | 300 |
| 3 | 4500 | 4 | 500 |

Output observed (the numbers after the prompts are the keyboard echo):

```
i = 1
Enter number of metres: 25
25m is equivalent to 0km and 25m

i = 2
Enter number of metres: 300
300m is equivalent to 0km and 300m

i = 3
Enter number of metres: 4500
4500m is equivalent to 4km and 500m
```

Pascal prints the same lines. After the third pass `i` becomes 4, the test `i <= 3` is false and the loop stops. One mark per correct result line.

questions.enonce_markdown: State what the program is designed to do.  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: The program is designed to **convert lengths given in metres into kilometres and metres, for three values entered by the user**. A `while` loop with a counter `i` repeats three times; in each pass it displays `i`, asks for a number of metres, divides it by 1000 to get the whole kilometres (quotient) and takes the remainder of the division by 1000 to get the metres left over, then displays "... m is equivalent to ... km and ... m". For example 4500 m gives 4 km and 500 m.

questions.enonce_markdown: The keyword "while", which is used in the program is an example of which programming construct? Explain how the stated programming construct works.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Programming construct: iteration (repetition, a loop)**, more precisely a **pre-test (condition-controlled) loop**.

**Explanation:** the condition in brackets (`i <= 3`) is evaluated **before** each pass. If it is true, the statements of the body (between `{ }` in C or `begin ... end` in Pascal) are executed, then control returns to the test; if it is false, the loop ends and the program continues after it. In this program `i` starts at 1 and is increased by 1 at the end of each pass (`i = i+1`), so the condition is true for i = 1, 2 and 3 and false for i = 4: the body is executed three times. (If the body never changed `i`, the loop would never stop.) One mark for naming iteration/loop, one mark for the explanation.
